\section[dauern]{dauern — to last, to take (time)}

\label{lesson:GE-C267-dauern}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for in time, then the German for at once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: dauern}
\textbf{dauern} — \textquotedblleft{}to last, to take (time)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Der Film dauerte drei Stunden.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The film lasted three hours.}
\end{quote}

Regular: \emph{es dauert}, \emph{es dauerte}, \emph{es hat gedauert}. \emph{Wie lange dauert das?} — how long does it take?

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dauern} comes from Middle High German \emph{dūren}, which was borrowed from Latin \emph{dūrāre} \textquotedblleft{}to last, to endure\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), itself built on \emph{dūrus} \textquotedblleft{}hard\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dauern}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dauern}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{dauern}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for in time, then the German for at once, then say \emph{dauern} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does dauern mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To last, to take (time)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[vergehen]{vergehen — to pass, to go by (of time)}

\label{lesson:GE-C267-vergehen}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for at once, then the German for to last.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: vergehen}
\textbf{vergehen} — \textquotedblleft{}to pass, to go by (of time)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Die Zeit verging sehr schnell.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The time went by very quickly.}
\end{quote}

Perfekt with \emph{sein}: \emph{Die Zeit ist schnell vergangen}. \emph{Vergangen} also means 'past'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vergehen} is built on \emph{gehen} \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Proto-Germanic \emph{gāną} (EtymDB), with the prefix \emph{ver-} \textquotedblleft{}away\textquotedblright{}: to go away, to pass.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vergehen}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{vergehen}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for at once, then the German for to last, then say \emph{vergehen} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[andauern]{andauern — to go on, to persist}

\label{lesson:GE-C267-andauern}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to last, then the German for to pass.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: andauern}
\textbf{andauern} — \textquotedblleft{}to go on, to persist\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Der Regen dauerte die ganze Nacht an.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The rain went on all night.}
\end{quote}

Separable: \emph{es dauert an}. \emph{Andauernd} means 'constantly'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{andauern} is built on \emph{dauern} \textquotedblleft{}to last\textquotedblright{}, from Middle High German \emph{dūren}, which was borrowed from Latin \emph{dūrāre} \textquotedblleft{}to last\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), with \emph{an} \textquotedblleft{}on\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[fortsetzen]{fortsetzen — to continue, to carry on with}

\label{lesson:GE-C267-fortsetzen}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to pass, then the German for to go on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: fortsetzen}
\textbf{fortsetzen} — \textquotedblleft{}to continue, to carry on with\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Nach der Pause setzten wir die Reise fort.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After the break we continued the journey.}
\end{quote}

Separable: \emph{wir setzen die Arbeit fort}, \emph{wir haben sie fortgesetzt}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fortsetzen} joins \emph{fort} \textquotedblleft{}forth, onward\textquotedblright{} and \emph{setzen} \textquotedblleft{}to set\textquotedblright{}, a cousin of English \emph{set} from Proto-Germanic \emph{satjaną} (EtymDB): to set forward.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[unterbrechen]{unterbrechen — to interrupt}

\label{lesson:GE-C267-unterbrechen}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to go on, then the German for to continue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: unterbrechen}
\textbf{unterbrechen} — \textquotedblleft{}to interrupt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ein Anruf unterbrach das Gespräch.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A phone call interrupted the conversation.}
\end{quote}

Not separable: \emph{er unterbricht}, \emph{er hat unterbrochen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{unterbrechen} joins \emph{unter} \textquotedblleft{}under, between\textquotedblright{} and \emph{brechen} \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{}, from Old High German \emph{brehhan}, Proto-Germanic \emph{brekaną} (EtymDB): to break in between.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
